Control the user entity must perform: User entities are responsible for designating at least two administrators for their tenant and for keeping the designated administrator list current.
Why CGI's control depends on it: Cypher Group Inc. acts on instructions from designated administrators only. If the list is stale, an instruction from a former administrator cannot be distinguished from a valid one.

Control the user entity must perform: User entities are responsible for enabling multi-factor authentication for all of their users, and for requiring phishing-resistant factors for their administrators.
Why CGI's control depends on it: The platform offers MFA; it does not force it. R-001 (phishing) lands on customer accounts through customer credentials, outside Cypher Group Inc.'s control.

Control the user entity must perform: User entities are responsible for reviewing their own users' access rights and roles at least quarterly and for removing access that is no longer required.
Why CGI's control depends on it: Cypher Group Inc. cannot know which of a customer's staff have left. Role assignment inside a tenant is a customer decision.

Control the user entity must perform: User entities are responsible for removing or disabling their users promptly when those users leave or change role, using the administrative console or the provisioning interface.
Why CGI's control depends on it: Deprovisioning is initiated by the customer. Cypher Group Inc. executes it; it does not trigger it.

Control the user entity must perform: User entities are responsible for reviewing the tenant audit log made available to them and for reporting anomalies to Cypher Group Inc. support.
Why CGI's control depends on it: Detection of misuse by a customer's own users depends on someone who knows what normal looks like inside that tenant.

Control the user entity must perform: User entities are responsible for reporting suspected security incidents affecting their tenant to Cypher Group Inc. without undue delay, using the published channel.
Why CGI's control depends on it: The incident clock in CGI-POL-005 s5.6.3 (GDPR 72 hours) starts when Cypher Group Inc. becomes aware. A customer who delays reporting consumes that budget.

Control the user entity must perform: User entities are responsible for determining what data they upload to the platform, and for not placing special categories of personal data, payment card numbers or regulated records in project content.
Why CGI's control depends on it: The platform is classified for customer account data, project content and limited personal data. It is not designed or assessed for special-category or cardholder data.

Control the user entity must perform: User entities are responsible for authorising, storing and rotating their own API keys and third-party integrations, and for revoking them when no longer required.
Why CGI's control depends on it: A customer-issued key carries the customer's authorisation. Cypher Group Inc. honours it and cannot judge whether it is still wanted.

Control the user entity must perform: User entities are responsible for issuing deletion or export instructions within their contractual window, and for retaining their own copies of exported data.
Why CGI's control depends on it: Deletion is performed on instruction. Retention beyond the platform is outside the system boundary.

Control the user entity must perform: User entities are responsible for the security of the devices and networks their users use to reach the platform.
Why CGI's control depends on it: Session hijacking or credential theft on a customer endpoint is indistinguishable at the platform from legitimate use.
